verdict.reason: Lagide is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should help the reef hold shape.

conversationalSummary.text: For TODAY, I’d do a check-first after work with a 16:30 start at Lagide, since it’s the best available option. The only catch is the wind angle looks poor for that spot, so it could get a bit messy even if the size is there. I’d check Surfline and the MEO Beachcam before leaving, and if it doesn’t look noticeably cleaner than expected, I’d skip.

best.explanation: Lagide looks like a fun-sized window for Fun progression, Medium confidence: 0.9-1.2 m, 170 kJ, 10 s period, consistent 68/100, and wind is the main risk.  A dependable left-hand reef that turns modest swell into real rides; this is best for clean, playful walls when the bigger beaches are too wild or too small; 10-13s at mid tide suits the reef shelves and gives long workable walls.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot.

ranked.explanation: Meio da Baia looks like a fun-sized window for Worth checking, Medium confidence: 0.9-1.2 m, 160 kJ, 7 s period, consistent 66/100, and wind is the main risk.  An inconsistent Baía spot that can work well when north-northwest swell reaches the bay; this is best for bodyboard sessions when the bay is clean, there is enough period and size, and the forecast shows a defined wave; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable.
